issues.description: The rule requires using Python 3.12+ modern type syntax (set[tuple[str, ...]] instead of Set[Tuple[str, ...]]), but the code imports and uses legacy typing module classes Set and Tuple

issues.title: Type mismatch in blocks_variable_output prevents variable blocking
issues.description: The blocks_variable_output method compares a Sequence (assigned_variable_selector) directly against a set of tuples (variable_selectors), but fails to convert the Sequence to a tuple first. This type mismatch causes the 'in' check to always return False, meaning the Variable Assigner node will never properly block streaming output of conversation variables. As a result, the response coordinator will incorrectly allow streaming to proceed before conversation variables are updated, violating the intended synchronization logic and potentially showing stale variable values to users.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
def blocks_variable_output(self, variable_selectors: Set[Tuple[str, ...]]) -> bool:
    """
    Check if this Variable Assigner node blocks the output of specific variables.

    Returns True if this node updates any of the requested conversation variables.
    """
    assigned_selector = self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector
    return assigned_selector in variable_selectors

issues.title: Incorrect input value used in NodeRunResult for CLEAR mode
issues.description: The code attempts to use updated_variable.to_object() for the CLEAR write mode's input value, but this represents the final cleared state rather than the input that triggered the operation. In CLEAR mode, income_value is actually the zero value generated by SegmentType.get_zero_value(), which is what should be shown as the input. This causes the NodeRunResult to misrepresent what value was used as input to the clear operation, breaking observability and potentially confusing downstream systems that rely on accurate input tracking.

issues.title: Test uses list equality instead of tuple conversion for event selector
issues.description: The test compares event.selector (which is a Sequence[str]) with a list literal using ==. While this might work in some cases due to Python's sequence equality, it's fragile and inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase. The original code correctly converted to tuple for comparison (tuple(event.selector) == ('conversation', 'conv_var')). This change breaks the filtering logic and will likely cause the test to fail to properly identify conversation variable chunk events, leading to false test failures.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
conv_var_chunk_events = [

    for event in events
    if isinstance(event, NodeRunStreamChunkEvent) and event.selector == ["conversation", "conv_var"]
]

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30832 - fix(api): defer streaming response until referenced variables are updated
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR makes the v1 Variable Assigner node report that it blocks output of the conversation variable it writes, so the response streaming coordinator waits for the write before streaming an Answer node that references that variable. The v2 node already implements this hook; v1 did not. The PR also adds a `blocks_variable_output` override on the v1 node, a v1 fixture (an assigner with no explicit `version`, which defaults to v1) and an integration test, and it changes the `inputs.value` recorded for CLEAR write mode.

The intent is sound and matches the existing v2 pattern, but the new v1 override is broken. It passes the assigned selector, a pydantic-validated `Sequence[str]` (a list), straight into a `set` of tuples. Membership on a set hashes the key first, so this raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. The coordinator calls this hook while building paths when the engine starts, so any v1 assigner on a path to a response node would fail. The new integration test uses exactly that shape, so it would fail too. I could not run the test suite here (dependencies are not installed), so the crash is established by tracing the call path and by reproducing the list-in-set behaviour in isolation, not by executing the test.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new v1 `blocks_variable_output` hashes a list against a set of tuples, which raises TypeError whenever a v1 Variable Assigner sits on a path to an Answer node. That is a crash in a path that previously worked, and it hits the PR's own new test. The out-of-scope CLEAR-mode change and the missing unit coverage for the hook should be addressed as well.

architecture.overview:
Answer and other response nodes stream their template text while the graph runs. `GraphEngine.start` calls `ResponseStreamCoordinator.register` for every RESPONSE node. Registration builds a paths map: it walks from the root to the response node and keeps the edges whose source node either is a BRANCH, CONTAINER or RESPONSE node, or returns True from `blocks_variable_output` for the variable selectors in the response template. Those edges are the points where streaming must wait.

The PR adds a `blocks_variable_output` override to the v1 `VariableAssignerNode`, matching the existing v2 override. When the v1 assigner writes a conversation variable that an Answer template references, the coordinator treats it as blocking and holds the Answer stream until the assigner has run. The change depends on the hook's argument types being compatible with the coordinator's `set[tuple[str, ...]]`, and the v1 implementation does not currently satisfy that.
steps: Entry point: `GraphEngine.start` registers each RESPONSE node with the coordinator (`api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_engine.py`, around line 345).

`ResponseStreamCoordinator._build_paths_map` collects template variable selectors as tuples, walks root-to-response paths, and asks each non-branch source node `blocks_variable_output(variable_selectors)` (`coordinator.py`, lines 172-221).

The base `Node.blocks_variable_output` returns False; the v2 assigner iterates its items and compares tuples. The PR adds the v1 counterpart in `variable_assigner/v1/node.py` by comparing `assigned_variable_selector` directly to the set. That value is a list, not a tuple, which is the defect.
CLEAR write mode now reports the zeroed variable's value in `inputs.value` instead of the unused input value. This is a separate behaviour change that the PR title does not mention.

The new fixture `test_streaming_conversation_variables_v1_overwrite.yml` wires Start to a v1 assigner (no `version`, so it defaults to '1') to an Answer that references `conversation.conv_var`. The new test asserts the streamed chunks equal the query value.

findings.title: v1 blocks_variable_output raises TypeError on list-vs-tuple membership
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, the new `blocks_variable_output` override (around lines 36-43) compares `self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector` (a list, from a pydantic `Sequence[str]` field) directly against `variable_selectors`, which is a `set[tuple[str, ...]]` built in `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/response_coordinator/coordinator.py` (around lines 172-175). Membership on a set hashes the key, so a list raises TypeError during engine startup whenever a v1 assigner precedes a response node. Convert the selector to a tuple before the membership check, matching the v2 implementation in `variable_assigner/v2/node.py` (lines 70-85). Keep the rest of the method unchanged, then run the new test `test_streaming_conversation_variables_v1_overwrite_waits_for_assignment` and the existing `test_streaming_conversation_variables` to confirm both pass.

findings.title: Unrelated CLEAR-mode change to recorded node inputs
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py` (around lines 102-111), the PR changed the `inputs.value` recorded for `WriteMode.CLEAR` to the zeroed variable's value. This is unrelated to the streaming fix in the PR title. Either revert this block so that `inputs.value` is always `income_value.to_object()`, or move it to a separate change with its own test that asserts the recorded input for clear operations. Do not change behaviour for over-write or append modes.

findings.title: No unit coverage for the v1 hook, so the crash went undetected
findings.fixPrompt: Add focused unit tests for `VariableAssignerNode.blocks_variable_output` in the v1 package, covering: a conversation-variable selector that matches a tuple in the set (expect True), one that does not match (expect False), and a non-conversation selector (expect False). Pass the set as `set[tuple[str, ...]]`, the same type the coordinator uses. Also set `version: '1'` explicitly on the assigner node in `api/tests/fixtures/workflow/test_streaming_conversation_variables_v1_overwrite.yml` so the v1 intent is clear. Follow the existing unit test layout under `api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/`.

findings.title: Typing imports diverge from the codebase style
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, replace the `typing.Set` and `typing.Tuple` usage in the new `blocks_variable_output` signature with built-in `set[tuple[str, ...]]`, and drop `Set, Tuple` from the `typing` import on line 2. This matches `api/core/workflow/nodes/base/node.py` and `variable_assigner/v2/node.py`.

findings.title: Follows the v2 pattern for response blocking
findings.body: The override matches the existing v2 `blocks_variable_output` contract, and its docstring accurately describes what the coordinator expects. Once the type issue is fixed, the change is small and sits where the coordinator already looks for blocking behaviour, so no coordinator changes are needed. The new integration test also reuses `TableTestRunner` and checks streamed chunk values, not just the final answer, which is the right observable for a streaming-ordering bug.
